judged_text: PostCreator now reads the render-pipeline bypass flag cook_method out of its public opts bag — the same bag Discourse's HTTP-facing post/topic creation endpoints populate from request params — so any logged-in user can submit cook_method=2 and have Post#cook return their raw HTML verbatim as `cooked`, skipping the markdown+sanitize pipeline (and the after_post_cook plugin filters). Arbitrary unsanitized HTML (including <script> tags) is persisted in `cooked` and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in topic views and the new embed iframe, giving any registered user a stored script-injection channel that the entire rendering architecture was built to prevent; a trusted-internal flag was welded onto a request-reachable constructor.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new bypass of the cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), and `PostCreator#setup_post` unconditionally assigns `post.cook_method = @opts[:cook_method]` if present (lib/post_creator.rb). There is no guard limiting who/what may set this option. Since views (including the newly added embed view) render HTML via `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), allowing arbitrary callers of `PostCreator` to choose `cook_method` creates a stored-XSS risk if any HTTP-facing code passes request params into PostCreator opts (the finding’s claim about endpoints isn’t shown in this diff, but the unguarded public option + raw-html cook path is verifiably introduced here).
